sections.h2: What is the quickest way to move a house in Hackensack?
sections.html:
A house moves fastest when few items are still open: a passed fire inspection, a settled tax balance and a price grounded in recent Hackensack sales. The city is the seat of Bergen County and its biggest municipality. It had 46,030 residents in 2020 and an estimated 46,380 on July 1, 2025.

Owners live in just 36.6 percent of homes, so rentals dominate. If you own a two-family house or small building, expect tenant, lease and rent questions during a sale. Whether you use an agent, a private buyer or a cash buyer, the city inspection, tax payoff and recording are the same. Cash only takes the lender's appraisal and approval out of the schedule.

Hackensack covers 4.35 square miles roughly 12 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan, and one block can look nothing like the next. The west side has single-family homes, a few on an acre or larger. Older central blocks have two-family houses, Prospect Avenue and the garden complexes offer apartment living at scale, and downtown has mixed-use buildings.

sections.h2: Figures that should shape your asking price
sections.html:
Hackensack pairs a renter-heavy population with a large tax bill: the average home was billed $10,307 in 2025.

Hackensack housing and tax figures
Local figureAmount
Population (July 1, 2025 estimate)46,380
Owner-occupied share of homes (2020 to 2024)36.6%
Typical owner-occupied home value$393,700
Typical monthly rent$1,911
Typical household income$84,277
Average assessment on a home, 2025$321,205
Average annual tax bill, 2025$10,307
Homes sold in the 2025 state study299, average price $396,963

The 2025 general tax rate is 3.209 per $100 and the effective rate is 2.527. Sales averaged around $75,000 over the average assessment. Let nearby closed sales, not the tax card, set your number.

sections.h2: Fire inspection before a Hackensack sale
sections.html:
Before closing, a seller needs the compliance certificate for smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and a portable fire extinguisher, which the Fire Prevention Bureau issues. The city form lists a $70 fee and a six-month validity period, and the certificate is issued the same day as the inspection.

A failed inspection, or an empty house at appointment time, means a new application and a new fee. Fill the form carefully with the buyer's name, the seller's name and the real estate company, because wrong details void the report.

The state Uniform Fire Code is the source, requiring a smoke alarm certificate when a one-family or two-family dwelling is sold, leased or changes occupants. Only the municipality can issue it. Get the house ready first:

  • Smoke alarms on each floor and in the basement, in shared stairwells and hallways, and within 10 feet of every sleeping area.
  • Sealed ten-year battery alarms in place of old ones, since the state Division of Fire Safety advises swapping alarms every decade.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm and a portable fire extinguisher, both listed on the city form.

The Building, Housing and Land Use department can tell you if your property type needs other resale paperwork.

Four installments are due each year, on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period after each. Interest on late balances is 8 percent a year up to $1,500 and 18 percent on the rest. Pay everything by November 10 to stay clear of the accelerated tax sale that starts November 11.

County recording can take three to six months before the city hears of a new owner, so a buyer should mail the collector an address after closing. As the seller, ask for a written balance before you review the closing statement.

If you believe the assessment is above market value, appeal to the Bergen County Board of Taxation, Two Bergen County Plaza in Hackensack, by the yearly April 1 date. Property assessed above $750,000 may skip ahead to the Tax Court, also by April 1.

When the deed is recorded, the seller owes the state Realty Transfer Fee, taken from a rate table keyed to the sale price. Above $1,000,000 a graduated percent fee also applies, with its own published schedule.

  • The state transfer fee, collected at recording.
  • The $70 fire certificate.
  • Mortgage payoff and any recorded liens.
  • Your share of the current quarter's property tax.

New Jersey residents sign the GIT/REP-3 so the clerk will accept the deed. Sellers from out of state prepay Gross Income Tax of no less than 2 percent of the price, unless a listed assurance covers them. Estates have a special case: an executor's deed to an heir named in the will is an exempt transfer, while a sale to an outside buyer is taxed and still needs the fire certificate.

sections.h2: How should a landlord handle a Hackensack rental sale?
sections.html:
Renters occupy roughly 63 percent of homes, at a typical rent of $1,911. The same Building, Housing and Land Use department staffs the Rent Stabilization Board, so find out whether your building is covered before you price from market rents.

The fire certificate is needed for leases as well as sales, so a new tenant and a sale may each trigger an inspection. Time yours so the six-month certificate is still good on closing day. An attorney should read every lease, since the buyer inherits the occupancy.

sections.h2: Roads and rail lines buyers use
sections.html: Interstate 80, Route 17, Route 4 and County Route 503 pass through, and the Hackensack River is crossed at Court Street, Midtown and Anderson Street. Pascack Valley Line trains stop at Anderson Street and Essex Street, heading to Hoboken and on to Penn Station New York. The Hackensack Bus Terminal sends buses to the Port Authority and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station. A listing close to a station or the terminal puts that commute in front of buyers.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a quick sale
sections.html: Schedule the fire inspection first, then request a written balance from the tax collector. Gather the deed, newest tax bill and any lease or payoff statement for your attorney. With the certificate in hand, a cash buyer can close on the date you both pick, and the attorney records the deed with the state filings. If tenants are staying, ask the buyer to confirm that in the contract, and if the house must be empty, set the move-out date in writing before you sign.

faqs.q: Is a fire inspection certificate mandatory for a Hackensack sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The state requires a smoke alarm certificate when a one- or two-family home sells. The city fire bureau issues it for $70, on a form that also covers carbon monoxide alarms and a fire extinguisher, and it lasts six months.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer fee on a Hackensack sale?
faqs.a: You do, at recording. The amount follows the state's schedule for your sale price, and only listed transfers, such as a deed from parent to child, are exempt.

faqs.q: Does a Hackensack house with unpaid taxes still sell?
faqs.a: It can, as long as the balance is cleared by closing. Current-year taxes should be paid by November 10 to avoid the tax sale starting November 11, and interest runs 8 percent up to $1,500 and 18 percent beyond.

faqs.q: May I sell while tenants live in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. Check rent stabilization with the Building, Housing and Land Use department and let an attorney review each lease.

faqs.q: What changes when the house came through an estate?
faqs.a: The estate completes a GIT/REP form for its residency status. A deed from the executor to an heir named in the will is exempt from the transfer fee, but a sale to an outsider is taxed and the fire certificate still applies.
